chapter: Our First Battle Wasn't a Total Loss
subtitle: 第一场仗，至少没有全输
sentences: Gu Huaichuan's letter kept me from sleeping properly all night.
Not because I was terrified.
I kept turning one question over in my head: if a page was missing from the government's records, was that a stroke of luck or what?
What if the clerk copying the book had simply fallen asleep?
I was still asking Wen Li that when we entered the Ministry of Punishments the next morning.
"Someone might have removed it on purpose," she said.
"Who?"
"I don't know."
"Why?"
"I don't know that either."
I sighed. "So we both got worked up over nothing last night."
"You were worked up?"
"I was so nervous I got up in the middle of the night and cursed Gu Huaichuan twice."
Right on cue, Gu Huaichuan opened the door and caught the second half of that sentence.
His face was perfectly blank. "Finished cursing me?"
"Good morning, Lord Gu." I straightened at once. "I was praising how thorough you are."
"By saying, 'He's driving me mad'?"
"...You have remarkably good hearing."
Wen Li turned toward the window. Her shoulders were shaking suspiciously hard.

We weren't the only visitors this time. Mother had come with Uncle Qin, carrying the original boat ticket dated the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. Its corners had been protected with waxed paper, and old water stains still marked its edges.
She held it close all the way there and only handed it to Uncle Qin at the duty-room door. "Ask how they'll examine it, who will receive it, and when we'll get it back. Don't miss a single word."

Gu Huaichuan didn't seem offended. With two clerks present, he recorded the paper, the color of the seal, the fold marks, and the name of the person presenting it. Then he asked Mother to confirm the faint scratch on the back herself.

"This proves only that the Jiang Trading House possesses this old ticket," he said when he finished. "Whether the seal was actually made at the time still has to be checked against the official seal impression and the wharf register."
Mother nodded. "I understand."

She didn't relax simply because Gu had agreed to examine it. The original stayed by his desk for preliminary inspection, but she wouldn't let go until she received a written receipt listing the ticket's condition, the date of acceptance, and the person responsible.
"Mother," I whispered, "don't you trust the Ministry?"
"I trust things that are clearly written down."
Gu heard her. Looking up, he said, "In that respect, your mother has more sense than you."
I was beginning to suspect that the mere sight of me gave this man a fresh supply of sarcasm.
Gu seated us along the corridor and spread out an inventory copied from the old case file.

"The North River supplementary register submitted to the Ministry three years ago had binding numbers, from A-One to A-Twelve. Only eleven pages remain in the case file. The missing one is A-Ten: the detailed grain receipts."
"So all we have left is the total of eight thousand shi?" Wen Li asked.

"The main register says eight thousand, and so does the supplementary receipt register. But the missing page should have listed who received the grain, which carts delivered it, and which granary gates they entered. Without that, we can't match the records to individual shipments."
I jabbed at the inventory. "Doesn't that make it obvious someone tore the page out?"
Gu shook his head. "It might have been left out when the book was bound three years ago, lost in transit, or removed later. The missing page is suspicious. It doesn't tell us who was responsible."
My pointing finger stopped in midair.
The man had an infuriating way of putting things.
Unfortunately, he was right.
Mother spoke up. "Is the original granary register still in North River?"
"We've drafted a formal request for it. If the original survives, we may be able to verify the figures. If that's missing too, we'll have to establish who had custody of it."
Wen Li stared at the words A-Ten on the table for a long while.

I knew what she was thinking. Her father had been jailed over a handover document saying eight thousand shi had reached the granary. Finding a gap in the evidence wouldn't erase a signature already on that document.
"Lord Gu." She raised her head. "When will my father be questioned again?"

"His next examination was scheduled for later this month, followed by a joint review. Now that we have a new boat ticket and a missing page to investigate, I'll submit a request to examine both before drawing conclusions solely from his old testimony."
"Can you promise that?"
"No."
Some color drained from her face.
Gu added, "I can promise to put the doubts in writing and submit them to the people authorized to decide. Whether a new review is approved will depend on their response."
Wen Li bowed her head.
"That is already more than enough. Thank you."
Something tightened in my chest as I watched.

In the original novel, Xie Linzhou only had to say, "I can save your father," and Wen Li was expected to marry him. In real life, just getting someone to examine a piece of paper properly meant running from office to office and thanking everyone along the way.
On the way back, Uncle Qin took us on a detour through the carriage yards in the west of the city.

The young worker from the Cen hauling agency had said yesterday that Yan Mancang was taken away in a gray-canopied carriage. Those were everywhere. But he remembered one detail: whenever the carriage crossed a threshold, its right rear wheel made a sharp click.
He had helped repair carriage wheels as a child. To his ear, the iron rim had an uneven joint.
It sounded insignificant to me, but Uncle Qin said, "A lad who can hear a faulty wheel is more useful than one who only remembers a color."
I thought about that. "Should we bring him here?"
"Not yet," Uncle Qin said. "First ask which carriage yards have recently repaired an iron rim."

We tried two yards with no luck. At the third, an elderly wheelwright was sharpening a blade in the courtyard. He listened without even looking up. "One came in the night before last. The iron rim on the right rear wheel was loose. We only returned it yesterday afternoon."
Wen Li asked immediately, "Whose carriage was it?"
"A hired one. The customer said he needed to pick up an elderly man. Paid well, too."
"Who hired it?"
"A tall steward in gray. He gave the surname Zhao. I didn't see any badge."
"Where did the carriage go?"
At last the old craftsman looked up. "Young ladies, what exactly are you asking for?"
I was about to say we were looking for someone, but Uncle Qin had already handed him an old receipt.

"This is the payment stub from a carriage the Jiang Trading House hired from your yard last year. I came because you keep proper accounts. If there's a record of that carriage's trip, please preserve it. If officials come asking, don't let the manager burn it as scrap paper."
He never mentioned the Marquis's residence or the relief grain.
The wheelwright studied the stub and slowly put down his sharpening stone.
"The manager keeps the accounts. I can't speak for him. But I repaired that carriage myself. I replaced the metal strip on its right rear wheel. If someone comes to ask, I can identify it."
Then he called through the doorway, "A-Kui! Find that old strip of iron. Don't throw it away!"
Wen Li glanced at Uncle Qin, who shook his head slightly to tell her not to press further.
Outside the yard, I was so excited I nearly clapped.
"We found it! That proves the Marquis's household abducted him!"
"It only proves someone hired that carriage," Wen Li said.

Uncle Qin continued, "We still need the Cen worker to identify the carriage, the yard to establish who hired it, and, if possible, records showing where it went that night. If even one link is missing, the Xie family can say it was another customer."
I lowered the hands I'd almost clapped together.
"Neither of you is particularly pleasant to listen to."
"If my lady wants to hear something pleasant," Uncle Qin said, "she should ask Chuntao when we get home."
"Even Chuntao has to ask Mother's permission before she compliments me these days!"
Wen Li doubled over laughing.
Once she recovered, she bowed solemnly to Uncle Qin. "Thank you. I'll send someone to Lord Gu tonight with the names of the wheelwright and the Cen worker, so they can give evidence."
"We can't just send someone to pass on a message," I reminded her. "We need names, addresses, and exactly what each person saw that day. Gu Huaichuan will make us fill out another form."
Uncle Qin looked at me and suddenly grinned.
"My lady, you really have learned something these last few days."
"What's that?"
"To leave a paper trail."
I wanted to argue. Then I remembered how I'd nearly taken the family's entire accounts into the Marquis's residence a few days earlier, and had to admit he had a point.
Three days later, word finally came from the Ministry.

The formal request for the North River granary register had been sent. The date of the old case's renewed examination would be set after the new evidence was checked. As for Yan Mancang, the Ministry had questioned people at both the Cen agency and the carriage yard. A witness confirmed that an elderly man had indeed been taken away earlier in a gray-canopied carriage, but no one had established whether the people who took him worked for the Marquis's household.
That was what several days of running around had earned us.
No dramatic declaration of innocence in court.
No Xie Linzhou dropping to his knees to confess.
We still didn't even know where Yan Mancang was.
I stared at the Ministry's written reply, which said, "Examination approved," for a long time.
"Does this count as a win?" I asked.
Wen Li stood beside me. Her eyes were a little red, but her voice was steady.
"It does."
"Your father's still in prison."
"I know."
She folded the reply neatly and tucked it close to her body.
"Before this, Xie Linzhou was the only person willing to say, 'I'll take care of your father's case.' Now there's finally something in the case file that I submitted myself."
I looked at her without speaking.
Then she held out a hand. "Come on. Let's get some candied hawthorn."
"Again?"
"You said the last ones were too sour."
"Then let's find a sweet batch."
"How are we supposed to tell just by looking?"
"Aren't you the one who's so good at planning? You planned me right into a bridal sedan. Picking a few sweet hawthorns should be easy."
Wen Li glared at me, then finally laughed.
We bought two skewers and walked all the way back to the Jiang residence.
I was planning to save the last half of mine for Chuntao. Then I looked up and saw a row of shop workers standing outside, silent and still.
Mother stood on the threshold with an official notice bearing the prefectural seal in her hand.
"Mother, what's happened?"
She handed it to me.

It stated that the old North River relief-grain case was being reexamined. The Jiang Trading House's old accounts room and related freight documents were to be sealed temporarily. Nothing was to be moved or destroyed, and anyone who had handled the records was required to appear when summoned.
I read it twice, my stomach sinking.
"They're only sealing the accounts room, right?"

"That's what the order says," Mother replied. "But three trading houses heard that Jiang Trading House was involved in the case, and all three canceled their scheduled cargo boats today. Two others are demanding early settlement of what we owe them."
"Isn't that just taking advantage of us while we're down?"
"Merchants aren't frightened by whether you're innocent or guilty. They're frightened of being dragged into trouble themselves."
The smile vanished from Wen Li's face beside me.
Anger burned in my chest. I turned to her. "Is Xie Linzhou behind this?"
"I don't know," she said. "The prefectural office may have lawful grounds to seal the records. As for who's spreading the rumors to profit from them, we'll have to investigate."
I knew she was right.
But knowing that didn't make it any easier to see the Jiang workers standing by the gate with their heads bowed.
Mother took the notice back and smoothed a crease at its corner.
"Mingyue, don't start an argument today."
"Mother..."

"If they seal the accounts room, or even force the rice shop to stop trading, I'll deal with it. But more than fifty workers need work to come back to tomorrow morning, and people will soon be demanding payment for the boats. If you really want to help, learn the names of the three reliable firms in the west of the city tonight. Tomorrow you'll go out with Uncle Qin."
I froze.
"Me?"
"Who else? You expect Xie Linzhou to do it?"
With that, she turned and went inside, ordering people to bring the abacus, light the lamps, and sort the inventory registers into three piles.
Wen Li offered me the candied-hawthorn skewer she was still holding.
"What's wrong?" she asked.
"I only just started feeling like we'd won something."
"We did win something," she said. "But Xie Linzhou isn't going to sit around and wait."
I looked down at the skewer. The sugar coating had gone sticky in the wind.
"Wen Li."
"Hmm?"
"Don't stand up for me tomorrow."
She looked startled.
"Why?"
"My mother's shops are mine to protect first. Just watch my back, and make sure nobody sells me out."
"That's a tall order."
"Wen Li!"
She laughed and stepped backward.
I laughed too, though I knew tomorrow wouldn't be easy.
The Jiang Mingyue from the original novel did nothing but orbit Xie Linzhou, fighting other women for him and accomplishing nothing else.
Well, look at me now.
I didn't even want the man anymore, and I had to learn how to collect debts for the Jiang family.
And this time, the original novel hadn't taught me a single thing.
translations: 顾怀川的信让我一夜没睡好。
不是因为太害怕。
是因为我翻来覆去都在想：官府的册子缺了一页，究竟算不算天降好消息？
万一只是抄书的人睡着了呢？
第二天进刑部时，我还在问温梨这个问题。
温梨说：“也可能是故意取走的。”
“谁取的？”
“不知道。”
“为什么取？”
“不知道。”
我叹了口气：“那咱俩昨晚都白激动了。”
“你激动了吗？”
“我紧张得半夜起来把顾怀川骂了两遍。”
正说着，顾怀川推门出来，正好听见后半句。
他面无表情：“骂完了吗？”
“顾大人早。”我立刻站直，“我是在夸您办事仔细。”
“夸人用‘烦死了’三个字？”
“……您听见的还挺全。”
温梨扭头去看窗外，肩膀抖得很厉害。
这次不止我们两个来。姜母带着秦叔，捧来那张十一月十八日的旧船票原件，票角压着蜡纸，边上还有几处当年沾的潮痕。
母亲一路都抱得紧紧的，到了值房门口才交给秦叔：“先问清楚怎么验，谁收，什么时候还。一个字都别落。”
顾怀川并未不耐烦。他请两名书吏在场，先照原票记下纸张、印色、折痕以及递呈人的姓名，又让母亲当面确认票背上那道浅浅的划痕。
“这只能证明姜记手上有这张旧票。”他写完说，“印是否当年所盖，还要和官存印模、码头簿核对。”
母亲点头：“我明白。”
她没有因为顾怀川答应查验就立刻放心。原票留在案边暂验，她坚持领了一张写明票样、收验日期和经手人的凭据，才肯放手。
我小声问她：“娘，您是不是不信刑部？”
“我信纸上写得清楚的东西。”
顾怀川听见了，抬头说：“这一点，令堂比你强。”
我怀疑他只要一见我，浑身就会长出刻薄人的力气。
顾怀川带我们到廊下坐定，将旧案的抄录清单摆在桌上。
“当年报到刑部的北河副册，纸尾有装订号，从甲一到甲十二。如今案卷里只有十一页。缺的是甲十，收粮细目。”
“所以只剩总数八千石？”温梨问。
“总册上记了八千，收粮副册也是八千。但缺失的细目本该列收粮人、车次和仓门，才好核对运的是哪一批。”
我指着清单：“这不是明摆着有人撕了吗？”
顾怀川摇头：“三年前装订时少了、转送途中遗落了，或是后来有人取走了，都有可能。缺页可疑，但不等于已经知道是谁干的。”
我手指一顿。
这人说话实在难听。
可他说得对。
母亲忽然问：“原仓册还在北河？”
“我们已经拟函调取。若原件尚存，总有机会核实。若也缺了，便要追问谁保管过。”
温梨望着桌上那行“甲十”，好一会儿没说话。
我知道她在想什么。她父亲当年正因为“八千石入仓”那张交接单被关了起来。如今证明东西不齐全，不代表能把签过的字也擦掉。
“顾大人。”她抬起头，“我父亲何时再审？”
“原定下旬复讯，随后由几司会核。如今有新的船票和副册缺页的疑点，我会上呈请求先验这两项，不宜只凭旧供定论。”
“您能保证吗？”
“不能。”
她脸色白了一下。
顾怀川补了一句：“我能保证写明疑点、呈给有权决定的人。至于是否准许重核，须等批复。”
温梨低头行了一礼。
“这样已经够了。多谢。”
我看得心里堵了一下。
原著里谢临舟只需说一句“我能救你父亲”，温梨就得嫁给他。现实里想让人认真核对一张纸，却要走这么多路，说这么多好话。
回去的路上，秦叔带我们绕到城西的车行。
昨日那个岑记伙计说过，带走严满仓的是辆灰篷车。满城灰篷车有的是，但他还记得一件小事：车行经过门槛时，右后轮总会发出“咔”的一声。
他小时候替人修过车轮，听得出来那是铁箍接缝不平。
这事听着不起眼，秦叔却说：“能听出车轮毛病的小子，比只会认颜色的有用。”
我若有所思：“那我们是不是该把他请来？”
“不急着叫。”秦叔说，“先问车行谁家的轮子刚补过铁。”
他们问了两家，都没有结果。到了第三家，修车的老师傅正在院里磨刀，听完描述，头也不抬地说：“前天夜里来过一辆，右后轮的铁箍松了，昨日下午才送回来。”
温梨立刻问：“谁家的车？”
“租出去的。客人说是去接一位老人，雇车钱给得足。”
“谁来租的？”
“一个高个子管事，穿灰衣，留了姓赵的名。牌子嘛，没看见。”
“车去了哪里？”
老师傅终于抬头：“姑娘，你们打听这些做什么？”
我刚想说找人，秦叔已经把手里的旧票递给他看。
“这是我们姜记去年在贵行定车的结账存根。你们车行肯记账，我才来问。这辆车若记了行程，烦请留着，日后官府有人查，别让掌柜当废纸烧了。”
他没有说侯府，也没有说赈粮。
老师傅看着那张存根，慢慢放下磨刀石。
“车行的账，掌柜收着。我做不了主。但那辆车我修过，右后轮的铁片是我亲手换的。谁要来问，我能认。”
他说完朝门内喊：“阿魁，把那块旧铁片找出来，别扔！”
温梨望向秦叔，秦叔微微摇头，示意她先别多问。
出了车行，我兴奋得差点拍手。
“找到了！那就能证明侯府抓人了！”
“只能证明有人雇了那辆车。”温梨说。
秦叔接着说：“还要让岑记那小伙子认车，让车行说清雇车人是谁，再看能不能查到这车那晚去了哪儿。一个环节接不上，谢家就能说是别的客人。”
我把差点拍下去的手收回来。
“你们两位说话真不讨人喜欢。”
“小姐要听好听的，”秦叔说，“回府问春桃去。”
“春桃现在夸我都要先请示我娘！”
温梨笑得直不起腰。
笑完后，她却郑重向秦叔行了礼：“多谢秦叔。今夜我会派人去找顾大人，把能作证的车行师傅和岑记伙计都报上去。”
“不能‘派人说一句’就算报上。”我提醒，“得把姓名、住址、当日见闻都写清。顾怀川准又要叫我们填单子。”
秦叔看着我，忽然乐了。
“小姐这几日，倒真学会一件事。”
“什么？”
“凡事想留个底。”
我想反驳，想想自己前些日子差点把全家的账带进侯府，只好认了。
三天后，刑部终于来了消息。
调取北河仓簿的公文已经发出；旧案的复讯将待新证核对后再定。至于严满仓，刑部已经分别向岑记脚行和车行核问，有人证实此前确有老人被灰篷车接走，但接走他的到底是不是侯府的人，还没有查清。
这是我们奔波数日换来的结果。
没有当堂喊冤得雪。
没有谢临舟跪地认罪。
甚至连严满仓在哪里，都还不知道。
我拿着那张写着“准予核验”的回帖，看了很久。
“这算赢了吗？”我问。
温梨站在旁边，眼圈有点红，声音却很稳。
“可你爹还在牢里。”
“我知道。”
她把回帖折得整整齐齐，贴身收好。
“以前只有谢临舟肯对我说，‘你爹的事我来办’。如今，案卷里终于有我自己递进去的东西了。”
我看着她，没有接话。
她忽然向我伸手：“走，吃糖葫芦。”
“又吃？”
“你上次说太酸。”
“这次挑甜的。”
“哪有一眼就能挑出甜的？”
“你不是很会算吗？连我都算进花轿，挑串山楂有什么难的？”
温梨瞪了我一眼，终于笑了。
我们买了两串，一路走到姜府门前。
我本想把剩下的半串留给春桃，抬头却看见铺子的伙计站了一排，谁也没说话。
我娘站在门槛上，手里捏着一张盖了府衙官印的告示。
“娘，怎么了？”
她把告示递给我。
上面写着：北河赈粮旧案重新核验，姜记商号旧账房及有关货票暂行封存，不许私自挪移、销毁；经手人员须随传随到。
我读了两遍，心里发沉。
“只是封账房？”
“文书写的是账房。”我娘说，“可城里三个商号听说姜记涉案，今日就把原定的货船退了。还有两家要我们提前结清银钱。”
“这不是趁火打劫吗？”
“做生意的人不怕你冤不冤。他们怕自己也被拖进去。”
温梨站在我身边，脸上的笑意已经没有了。
我心里憋着一股火，转头问她：“这是不是谢临舟干的？”
“不知道。”她说，“府衙要查账，本身也可能依法封存。至于谁趁机放风声，得查。”
我知道她说得对。
可道理归道理，看见姜家的伙计垂着头站在门边，还是觉得胸口发紧。
母亲把告示从我手里拿回去，抚平了角上的折痕。
“明月，今天先别吵。”
“账房能封，米铺能停，我认。但明早五十多个伙计得开工，晚些还有人来催船钱。你若真想帮忙，今夜把城西三家熟行的名字认全，明日跟秦叔出去跑。”
我怔住。
“不是你，难道还指望谢临舟？”
她说完就转身进门，吩咐人搬算盘、点灯、把存货册分成三摞。
温梨把手里那串糖葫芦递给我。
“怎么了？”她问。
“刚刚才觉得赢了一回。”
“本来也赢了。”她说，“只是谢临舟也不会坐着等。”
我低头看了看那串糖葫芦，山楂上的糖衣已经被风吹得发黏。
“温梨。”
“明天你别替我出头。”
她愣了一下。
“为什么？”
“我娘的铺子，得先由我来守。你帮我看着，别让我被人卖了就行。”
“那倒难。”
“温梨！”
她笑着往后退了一步。
我也笑了，却知道明日不会轻松。
原著的姜明月只会围着谢临舟转，除了抢人，什么都不干。
现在倒好。
我连他都不想要了，却得先学会替姜家讨账。
而这回，原著里半个字也没教过我。

annotations.explain: keep someone from doing something 表示阻止某人做某事，这里不是主动不让睡，而是心事使人失眠。
annotations.example: The noise kept me from sleeping.

annotations.explain: Not because ... 常用来否定读者预期的原因，后面常跟真正原因，小说里可独立成句制造节奏。
annotations.example: Not because I was angry, but because I was worried.

annotations.phrase: turning one question over in my head
annotations.meaning: 脑子里反复琢磨一个问题
annotations.explain: turn something over in one's head 是反复思考、掂量，并非字面翻转。
annotations.example: I've been turning your suggestion over in my head.

annotations.explain: stroke of luck 是固定名词短语，常带突然碰上好事的意味。
annotations.example: Finding the keys was a stroke of luck.

annotations.explain: What if + 句子可以提出假设、担心或另一种解释，读小说时要看人物是焦虑还是推理。
annotations.example: What if we're wrong?

annotations.explain: fall asleep 强调从清醒进入睡眠的变化；be asleep 表示已经睡着的状态。
annotations.example: He fell asleep during the lecture.

annotations.explain: was still doing 用过去进行时突出当时动作持续未停，与 when 从句形成时间交叠。
annotations.example: I was still working when she called.

annotations.explain: on purpose 是日常高频固定表达，与 by accident（偶然地）相对。
annotations.example: She didn't break it on purpose.

annotations.explain: either 放在否定句末表示“也”，不同于肯定句中常见的 too。
annotations.example: I don't know the answer either.

annotations.explain: get worked up 指因紧张、生气或兴奋而情绪上头，不等于单纯工作很忙。
annotations.example: Don't get worked up over a rumor.

annotations.meaning: 为没什么实际结果的事
annotations.explain: over + 名词可指出情绪的起因；over nothing 带“白折腾”的判断。
annotations.example: They argued over nothing.

annotations.explain: so + 形容词 + (that) 从句可表达程度引出的结果；这里 that 被省略。
annotations.example: I was so tired I forgot my keys.

annotations.phrase: in the middle of the night
annotations.explain: in the middle of the night 是常用时间短语，比 at night 更突出深夜时段。
annotations.example: The phone rang in the middle of the night.

annotations.meaning: 说曹操曹操到；恰好按点出现
annotations.explain: right on cue 表示像听到提示一样恰好出现，常用于幽默的巧合。
annotations.example: Right on cue, the lights went out.

annotations.explain: catch 在听力语境中可表示听见、听清或捕捉信息，而非“抓住”。
annotations.example: Sorry, I didn't catch the last part.

annotations.explain: blank 形容表情时指没有流露情绪，不是“空白脸”直译。
annotations.example: She gave me a blank look.

annotations.explain: straighten 在这里是不及物动词，描述身体姿态突然端正，常暗示紧张或尊敬。
annotations.example: He straightened when the teacher entered.

annotations.explain: how + 形容词 + 主语 + 谓语构成感叹或宾语从句，强调程度。
annotations.example: I appreciate how careful you are.

annotations.explain: by + doing 表示方式、手段，适用于解释怎么做某事。
annotations.example: She learned by making mistakes.

annotations.explain: remarkably 用来强调超出寻常；good hearing 指听觉灵敏，不是“良好听证”。
annotations.example: My grandfather has remarkably good hearing.

annotations.explain: turn toward 表示朝某个方向转身或转脸，也可比喻转向某种选择。
annotations.example: She turned toward the door.

annotations.explain: suspiciously 在此带叙述者揶揄，暗示温梨其实在憋笑。
annotations.example: He was suspiciously quiet all morning.

annotations.explain: not the only ... 用否定结构表达“还有其他人”，常用于叙事引入新人物。
annotations.example: You weren't the only one who noticed.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时被动 had been + 过去分词提示动作发生于当前叙述之前。
annotations.example: The paintings had been covered with cloth.

annotations.explain: stain 既可以指名词污迹，也可作动词“弄脏”；water stain 强调水留下的痕迹。
annotations.example: There were water stains on the ceiling.

annotations.explain: hold something close 指贴身紧抱，体现珍视或担忧，不是抽象的“关系亲密”。
annotations.example: She held the photograph close.

annotations.explain: not ... a single ... 强调一个也不，语气比 not any 更强。
annotations.example: Don't miss a single detail.

annotations.explain: with + 名词 + 形容词/分词可表达伴随情形；present 在这里是“在场”，不是“礼物”。
annotations.example: With everyone present, the meeting began.

annotations.explain: ask someone to do something 是常见宾语补足语结构，不能说 ask someone do。
annotations.example: They asked me to sign here.

annotations.explain: faint 可形容痕迹、声音或颜色不明显，不只表示“晕倒”。
annotations.example: I noticed a faint mark on the wall.

annotations.explain: prove only that 通过 only 限定证据能支持的结论，避免推论过度。
annotations.example: The receipt proves only that a payment was made.

annotations.explain: check against 是将材料与参照物核对，不等于简单 check（查看）。
annotations.example: Check the figures against the original report.

annotations.phrase: whether the seal was actually made
annotations.explain: whether 引导间接疑问，表示仍待判断的两种可能，不能预设为真。
annotations.example: We need to know whether it was signed.

annotations.explain: simply because 表示某一理由不足以成立，常与否定主句搭配。
annotations.example: Don't trust him simply because he's friendly.

annotations.explain: let go 可以指放开具体物品，也常比喻放下担忧或执念。
annotations.example: She wouldn't let go of the envelope.

annotations.explain: 现在分词 listing 后置修饰 receipt，说明凭据载有哪些细节。
annotations.example: He handed me a note listing the costs.

annotations.explain: 否定疑问句可能表达意外、质疑或寻求确认，语气要结合关系判断。
annotations.example: Don't you trust me?

annotations.explain: write down 是常见短语动词，强调把口头或心里的信息记为文字。
annotations.example: Write down the phone number.

annotations.explain: in that respect 用于限定评价范围，比笼统地说 in general 精确。
annotations.example: In that respect, the plans are similar.

annotations.explain: have sense 指有常识、判断力，more sense than 比较的是理性程度。
annotations.example: She has more sense than I do.

annotations.explain: supply 原指供应量，这里与 sarcasm 搭配成幽默隐喻，非字面物品。
annotations.example: He seemed to have an endless supply of excuses.

annotations.explain: spread out 是常见短语动词，可指文件摊开、人群分散或空间延展。
annotations.example: She spread out the maps on the table.

annotations.explain: file 在法律行政语境中是卷宗或档案，与计算机文件的意义不同。
annotations.example: The evidence is in the case file.

annotations.explain: submit something to an authority 表示向机构正式提交，带程序性质。
annotations.example: Submit your report to the office.

annotations.explain: remain 强调剩余状态；Only 提前突出少于应有数量。
annotations.example: Only two tickets remain.

annotations.explain: one 替代前文的单数名词 page，避免重复。
annotations.example: I found one book, but the missing one is still lost.

annotations.explain: all + (that) 从句可作名词性结构；have left 表示“还剩下”。
annotations.example: This is all we have left.

annotations.explain: so + 助动词 + 主语构成倒装，表示前面肯定情况同样适用于另一对象。
annotations.example: She likes tea, and so does he.

annotations.explain: should have + 过去分词表示过去应发生但实际可能未发生的情况。
annotations.example: The report should have listed all the names.

annotations.explain: match A to B 指把两类事物一一匹配，用于数据、证据、身份核对。
annotations.example: Match each payment to an invoice.

annotations.explain: make + 宾语 + 形容词构成使役结构；在反问中可表达强烈主观判断。
annotations.example: Doesn't this make it obvious?

annotations.explain: leave out 指有意或无意排除某部分，常用于名单、报告、叙述。
annotations.example: You left out an important detail.

annotations.explain: in transit 是物流和证据移交中的固定表达，说明处于运输途中。
annotations.example: The parcel was lost in transit.

annotations.explain: it doesn't tell us ... 用于限定信息所能支持的推断。
annotations.example: The photo doesn't tell us who took it.

annotations.explain: in midair 描写动作突然停住，比 stopped 更有画面感。
annotations.example: Her hand froze in midair.

annotations.explain: have a way of doing 表示某人做事一贯有某种特点，常含评价。
annotations.example: He has a way of making me laugh.

annotations.explain: 句首副词可表达叙述者态度；这里承认对方正确却并不开心。
annotations.example: Unfortunately, she was right.

annotations.explain: speak up 指主动开口，也可表示声音大一点或为立场发声。
annotations.example: Someone finally spoke up at the meeting.

annotations.explain: formal 在行政语境中强调程序和形式合规，不等于语气生硬。
annotations.example: They sent a formal request for the records.

annotations.explain: survive 可用于文件、建筑等事物“保存至今”，不只说人活下来。
annotations.example: Few documents from that period survive.

annotations.explain: have custody of 在法律与行政语境中表示实际保管或监护责任。
annotations.example: The clerk had custody of the evidence.

annotations.explain: for a while 表示一会儿，long 加强时长且偏叙事语气。
annotations.example: She remained silent for a long while.

annotations.explain: be jailed over something 表示因某事件卷入牢狱，不等于因已被证明有罪。
annotations.example: He was jailed over the disputed transaction.

annotations.explain: erase 本义擦除，在此比喻不能消除已有签名或既成事实。
annotations.example: One apology won't erase the damage.

annotations.explain: 被动语态 be questioned 表示被官方或他人询问，强调接受问讯者。
annotations.example: The witness will be questioned again.

annotations.explain: be scheduled for 是常用计划表达，不代表事情已发生。
annotations.example: The hearing was scheduled for Friday.

annotations.explain: followed by 是顺序表达；过去分词短语可以紧凑连接程序步骤。
annotations.example: The lecture was followed by questions.

annotations.explain: draw a conclusion 是固定搭配，比 make a conclusion 更地道。
annotations.example: We shouldn't draw conclusions too early.

annotations.explain: solely 强调排他性的唯一依据，适合推理或证据讨论。
annotations.example: Don't judge a case solely from one statement.

annotations.phrase: Some color drained from her face
annotations.explain: color drained from someone's face 是文学描写，表示受惊、失望或打击。
annotations.example: The color drained from his face.

annotations.explain: put something in writing 指书面记载以便留证据，重要的不只是说出口。
annotations.example: Please put the agreement in writing.

annotations.explain: be authorized to do 强调正式授权，区别于有能力 can。
annotations.example: Only the manager is authorized to approve it.

annotations.explain: depend on 表示结果由条件决定，是高频搭配。
annotations.example: The outcome will depend on the evidence.

annotations.explain: more than enough 强调超过最低需要，此处含克制的感激。
annotations.example: You've done more than enough.

annotations.explain: 胸口紧缩是心理感受的文学化表达，不一定指医学上的胸痛。
annotations.example: Something tightened in my chest when I heard it.

annotations.explain: be expected to 可表示社会规范下的期待，也可表示职责与义务。
annotations.example: Employees are expected to arrive on time.

annotations.phrase: meant running from office to office
annotations.explain: mean + doing 表示意味着采取某行为；不是 mean to do（打算做）。
annotations.example: Fixing this means starting again.

annotations.explain: along the way 既可指旅途途中，也可指完成目标的整个过程。
annotations.example: I learned a lot along the way.

annotations.explain: on the way back 是日常路线表达，back 表示返回原处。
annotations.example: We stopped for tea on the way back.

annotations.explain: take someone on a detour through 表示不走直路而经某地。
annotations.example: We took a detour through the old town.

annotations.explain: had said 过去完成时用于相对于另一个过去时间点更早的说话行为。
annotations.example: She had said yesterday that she was leaving.

annotations.explain: be everywhere 是口语化的泛指，强调数量多、不具唯一识别价值。
annotations.example: Those blue bags are everywhere.

annotations.explain: whenever 表示每次……都，比 when 强调重复性。
annotations.example: The door creaked whenever it opened.

annotations.explain: to one's ear 表示从听觉判断，常用于口音、声音和机械故障。
annotations.example: To my ear, the engine sounds different.

annotations.explain: uneven 可形容表面不平、分布不均、节奏不稳定。
annotations.example: The floor had an uneven joint.

annotations.explain: sound + 形容词是系动词用法，不加 be。
annotations.example: The problem sounds simple.

annotations.explain: 比较级 + than；用于强调提供信息的质量，不是外在显眼程度。
annotations.example: A clear note is more useful than a guess.

annotations.explain: think about 表示考虑某事；think of 更常涉及想起或提出想法，二者有交叉但不完全相同。
annotations.example: I'll think about your proposal.

annotations.explain: not yet 指某事现在尚未发生或时机未到，并非永不。
annotations.example: Are you ready? Not yet.

annotations.explain: recently 和完成时经常同现，修饰不久前的经历。
annotations.example: They've recently repaired the bridge.

annotations.explain: with no luck 是口语固定表达，说明尝试未成功。
annotations.example: We searched all day with no luck.

annotations.explain: without + doing 表示没有伴随某动作；even 强化“连……都不”。
annotations.example: She answered without even looking up.

annotations.explain: the night before last 表示相对于说话时间的前天夜里，区别于 last night 昨晚。
annotations.example: I got home the night before last.

annotations.explain: one 替代前面提到的 carriage；hire 表示雇用、租用。
annotations.example: We used a hired car.

annotations.explain: 省略主语的短句在口语叙事中常见，实际意思是客人支付了足够的钱。
annotations.example: The job paid well.

annotations.explain: give a name / surname 指向登记方提供姓名或姓氏，不证明身份真实。
annotations.example: He gave a false surname.

annotations.explain: didn't see 和 there was no 不同：前者说明观察不到，不能证明客观不存在。
annotations.example: I didn't see any sign of damage.

annotations.phrase: what exactly are you asking for
annotations.explain: what exactly ... 加强追问，ask for 指请求、索取信息或物品。
annotations.example: What exactly are you asking for?

annotations.explain: be about to + 动词表示紧接着就要发生的动作，常被 but 打断。
annotations.example: I was about to leave when he called.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时突出另一个过去动作发生前已完成的行为。
annotations.example: He had already left by the time I arrived.

annotations.explain: stub 指票据或支票上留作记录的存根，也常用于纸质收据。
annotations.example: Keep the payment stub for your records.

annotations.explain: keep accounts 是固定动宾搭配，proper 强调记录可靠、规范。
annotations.example: The company keeps proper accounts.

annotations.phrase: don't let the manager burn it
annotations.explain: let + 宾语 + 动词原形，不能用 to burn；表达允许或阻止某人做某事。
annotations.example: Don't let anyone change the file.

annotations.explain: as + 名词短语表示把某物视作某种用途或身份。
annotations.example: They sold the sheets as scrap paper.

annotations.explain: never 比 didn't 更绝对，表示在整个过程里一次也没提及。
annotations.example: She never mentioned the price.

annotations.explain: put down 是高频短语动词，可表示放下物品、记录、贬低等，需看宾语判断。
annotations.example: Put down the pen for a moment.

annotations.explain: speak for somebody 指代表某人发言或决定，不等于与他交谈。
annotations.example: I can't speak for the whole team.

annotations.explain: 条件从句用一般现在时表达将来可能情形，主句可用 can。
annotations.example: If anyone calls, I can help.

annotations.explain: throw away 是可分离短语动词，代词宾语 it 必须放在中间。
annotations.example: Don't throw the receipt away.

annotations.explain: press someone / press further 表示施压或继续追问，不是“按压更远”。
annotations.example: I decided not to press further.

annotations.explain: nearly + 动词表示几乎做了但未真正发生；与 actually did 相反。
annotations.example: I nearly cried with relief.

annotations.explain: prove 用于宣称证据足以支持结论；这一句展示角色过度推断。
annotations.example: A signature alone doesn't prove fraud.

annotations.explain: only 限定证据范围，直接反驳上句的过度推断。
annotations.example: It only proves the door was opened.

annotations.explain: if possible 常作插入语，省略 it is，不代表已经能够做到。
annotations.example: Send the original, if possible.

annotations.phrase: If even one link is missing
annotations.explain: link 比喻证据链的一环；条件句强调脆弱的推论链。
annotations.example: If one link is missing, the argument weakens.

annotations.phrase: can say it was another customer
annotations.explain: can say 在此是提出抗辩解释的可能性，不等于结论被证实。
annotations.example: They can say it was a mistake.

annotations.explain: lower 是及物动词，描述身体动作，衬托人物兴奋突然泄气。
annotations.example: He lowered his hand slowly.

annotations.explain: pleasant to + 动词不定式表示做某件事时给人的体验。
annotations.example: The news wasn't pleasant to hear.

annotations.explain: when 引导将来时间从句时通常用一般现在时，不用 will get。
annotations.example: Call me when you get home.

annotations.explain: before 后可接完整从句，强调先后次序。
annotations.example: Think before you speak.

annotations.explain: double over 描述因笑或痛而弯腰，后面可接 laughing 表伴随原因。
annotations.example: We doubled over laughing at the joke.

annotations.explain: once 引导时间从句，表示“一……就”或“等……之后”，不是一次。
annotations.example: Once you recover, we'll talk.

annotations.explain: solemnly 强调庄重、认真，与此前大笑形成情绪转变。
annotations.example: He nodded solemnly.

annotations.explain: pass on 表示转告、传递消息；与 hand over（交出实物）不同。
annotations.example: Please pass on my thanks.

annotations.explain: fill out 是完整填写表格；fill in 常用于填写具体空格，二者部分场景可互换。
annotations.example: Fill out the form before Friday.

annotations.explain: these last few days 表示延续到目前的一段最近时期，常与现在完成时同现。
annotations.example: I've been busy these last few days.

annotations.meaning: 留下可追溯的书面记录
annotations.explain: paper trail 是惯用表达，指使交易、决策、调查过程有据可查，不限纸张。
annotations.example: Always leave a paper trail for approvals.

annotations.explain: had nearly + 过去分词强调在叙事参照时间之前险些做出某事。
annotations.example: I'd nearly forgotten the meeting.

annotations.explain: have a point 是口语固定表达，承认对方理由成立，不等于完全同意其立场。
annotations.example: I don't like it, but you have a point.

annotations.explain: word came 里的 word 指消息、音讯，而非某个单词。
annotations.example: Word came that the roads were open.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时被动强调正式请求已在回报之前发送，不表示已经收到原册。
annotations.example: The documents had been sent earlier.

annotations.explain: as for 用于转换讨论焦点，常引出另一人或另一议题。
annotations.example: As for tomorrow, we can decide later.

annotations.explain: indeed 强调证实某一有限事实，过去完成时被动说明动作已发生。
annotations.example: The package had indeed been delivered.

annotations.explain: establish whether 在法律或调查中指查证是否成立，不应等同 assume。
annotations.example: We haven't established whether it's genuine.

annotations.explain: run around 可指为办事四处跑，不一定真的奔跑。
annotations.example: I've been running around all day.

annotations.explain: 小说使用省略谓语的名词片段，连续列举期待落空，形成节奏。
annotations.example: No applause. No celebration. Just silence.

annotations.explain: drop to one's knees 表示迅速跪下，常用于戏剧化场面。
annotations.example: He dropped to his knees in relief.

annotations.explain: not even 表示连最低预期都没有达到，强化挫败感。
annotations.example: I didn't even know her name.

annotations.explain: stare at 常表示盯着看一段时间，可能有疑惑、震惊或出神。
annotations.example: She stared at the letter.

annotations.explain: for + 一段时间强调动作持续时间。
annotations.example: We waited for a long time.

annotations.explain: count as 表示被认作某种类别或结果；并非字面数数。
annotations.example: Does that count as progress?

annotations.phrase: Her eyes were a little red
annotations.explain: eyes were red 常暗示哭过或将哭，语境不一定明确说明原因。
annotations.example: His eyes were red, but he smiled.

annotations.phrase: tucked it close to her body
annotations.explain: tuck 可指塞入、掖好，突出小心保存或私密性。
annotations.example: She tucked the note into her coat.

annotations.explain: take care of 除“照顾人”还可指负责解决事情，具体程度需要看上下文。
annotations.example: I'll take care of the paperwork.

annotations.explain: something in the case file 强调进入正式记录，与私下承诺形成对比。
annotations.example: Your statement is now in the case file.

annotations.explain: myself 在这里是强调代词，强调由本人而非替她承诺的男子提交。
annotations.example: I wrote the letter myself.

annotations.explain: hold out 可指伸出手、递出物品，也可指坚持不让步，需按宾语判断。
annotations.example: He held out a hand to help.

annotations.explain: batch 指一批次制作或采摘的东西，常用于食品、商品、数据。
annotations.example: This batch of apples is sweeter.

annotations.explain: just by + doing 表示仅凭某种方式，强调依据不足。
annotations.example: You can't tell just by looking.

annotations.explain: right into 加强方向或结果的直接性；此处是半开玩笑地指被设计进局。
annotations.example: The plan pushed me right into trouble.

annotations.explain: should 这里是根据经验作预期判断，不是表示强制义务。
annotations.example: That should be easy enough.

annotations.explain: glare at 带怒意或责怪；stare at 只是长时间注视，不必含怒。
annotations.example: She glared at him across the table.

annotations.explain: all the way 表示完整路程或程度，强调没有中断。
annotations.example: We walked all the way home.

annotations.explain: was planning to 描述过去的计划，接着可能出现打断计划的事件。
annotations.example: I was planning to call you.

annotations.explain: look up 是抬眼、抬头看，后接 and saw 使镜头转到突然发现。
annotations.example: I looked up and saw a stranger.

annotations.explain: bearing 是 bear 的现在分词，意为带有、印有，不是“忍受”。
annotations.example: He showed a letter bearing the official seal.

annotations.explain: 过去进行时被动 was being + 过去分词表示在过去某时正在进行的程序。
annotations.example: The case was being reviewed.

annotations.explain: be to + 被动式常用于正式通知、规定的未来安排。
annotations.example: The records are to be preserved.

annotations.explain: when summoned = when they are summoned，省略共同主语和 be 动词。
annotations.example: Appear in court when summoned.

annotations.explain: one's stomach sinks 是面对坏消息时的身体化情绪表达。
annotations.example: My stomach sank when I saw the bill.

annotations.explain: that's what ... says 说明文件字面范围，暂不推论外部效果。
annotations.example: That's what the contract says.

annotations.explain: demand + 名词/动名词可表示强硬要求，settlement 在商业中指结算偿付。
annotations.example: The supplier demanded early payment.

annotations.explain: take advantage of somebody 常有利用弱势处境之意；take advantage of an opportunity 可为中性。
annotations.example: Don't take advantage of their trust.

annotations.explain: be down 在这里指处境困难，非字面躺着；while 引导同时性。
annotations.example: They helped us while we were down.

annotations.explain: drag somebody into 强调不情愿地卷入纠纷或坏事。
annotations.example: Don't drag her into this dispute.

annotations.explain: vanish 描写瞬间消失，比 stop smiling 更有画面变化。
annotations.example: The smile vanished from his face.

annotations.explain: be behind something 可表示支持，也可表示在幕后推动，语境决定褒贬。
annotations.example: Who was behind the leak?

annotations.explain: grounds 指某行为的根据，常用于法律、行政判断。
annotations.example: They had grounds to reopen the case.

annotations.explain: as for + 疑问词从句引出尚待调查的问题，而非下结论。
annotations.example: As for who paid, nobody knows.

annotations.explain: 人物认同对方判断但仍可能情绪不安，体现理性与情感并存。
annotations.example: I knew he was right.

annotations.explain: make it easier 表示使处境更容易承受；否定结构表达理性无法消除痛苦。
annotations.example: Knowing why didn't make it easier.

annotations.explain: with + 名词 + 过去分词描述伴随状态，bowed 是低垂的结果状态。
annotations.example: They stood with their heads bowed.

annotations.explain: smooth 作动词表示抚平；crease 指纸张或衣服上的褶痕。
annotations.example: She smoothed the crease in the paper.

annotations.explain: start an argument 指挑起争论；argument 可指口角也可指论证，看语境。
annotations.example: Let's not start an argument now.

annotations.explain: deal with 用于处理问题、应对人或情境，是高频短语动词。
annotations.example: I'll deal with the complaint.

annotations.phrase: If you really want to help
annotations.explain: if + 一般现在时可提出实际条件；really 加强对动机的要求。
annotations.example: If you want to help, listen first.

annotations.explain: go out with 在这里是一起外出，其他语境也可表示恋爱交往，要结合角色关系。
annotations.example: I'll go out with the team tomorrow.

annotations.explain: Who else? 可作反问，暗示答案已很清楚。
annotations.example: Who else could do it?

annotations.phrase: expect Xie Linzhou to do it
annotations.explain: expect someone to do something 是常用搭配，这里的反问带讽刺。
annotations.example: Do you expect me to pay for everything?

annotations.explain: With that 常作叙事过渡，接人物离场或新行动。
annotations.example: With that, she closed the door.

annotations.explain: sort 可以指分类整理；inventory 指库存或存货清单。
annotations.example: Sort the files by date.

annotations.explain: offer someone something 为双宾语结构，主动提出给予，不强制接受。
annotations.example: She offered me a seat.

annotations.explain: only just 强调动作发生得非常近，常带来不及享受就被打断的意味。
annotations.example: I'd only just sat down when it rang.

annotations.explain: sit around 表示无所事事地耗时间，与后接 wait 构成口语化强调。
annotations.example: We can't sit around and wait forever.

annotations.explain: go + 形容词可表示状态变化，常用于 go bad、go cold、go wrong。
annotations.example: The bread had gone stale.

annotations.explain: stand up for somebody 是维护、支持某人，不是字面从椅子上站起来。
annotations.example: She stood up for her friend.

annotations.explain: look + 形容词是系动词结构；startled 指突如其来的惊讶。
annotations.example: He looked startled by the news.

annotations.explain: be someone's to do 表示某项责任或决定归某人承担。
annotations.example: It's your choice to make.

annotations.explain: watch someone's back 是口语惯用表达，指照应、保护而非真的盯着后背。
annotations.example: Don't worry; I'll watch your back.

annotations.explain: sell someone out 表示背叛信任、为私利出卖他人，是常见短语动词。
annotations.example: He sold out his friends for money.

annotations.meaning: 强人所难；难完成的要求
annotations.explain: a tall order 是习语，表示要求太高或任务艰巨，与高矮无关。
annotations.example: Finishing by noon is a tall order.

annotations.explain: step backward 指身体后退，也可比喻倒退，文中伴随调侃的动作。
annotations.example: She stepped backward and laughed.

annotations.explain: wouldn't 是过去时视角中的将来预测，与叙述者当时的预感一致。
annotations.example: I knew the next day wouldn't be easy.

annotations.explain: do nothing but + 动词原形强调行为单一，含批评意味。
annotations.example: He did nothing but complain.

annotations.explain: orbit 原指绕轨道运行，比喻把人生重心完全放在某人身上。
annotations.example: She refused to orbit his career anymore.

annotations.explain: 固定口语句子可带自嘲、对比过去或自豪，取决于上下文。
annotations.example: I used to hate cooking. Look at me now!

annotations.explain: not even 加强否定，强调比预期更极端的变化。
annotations.example: I don't even want an explanation.

annotations.explain: learn how to + 动词原形说明掌握具体技能或方法。
annotations.example: I need to learn how to negotiate.

annotations.phrase: hadn't taught me a single thing
annotations.explain: not a single thing 强调零信息；过去完成时呼应原著在当前场景之前的内容。
annotations.example: The guide hadn't told us a single thing.
